title: Asian Games 2026 Cricket Draw Confirmed: India Get Direct Knockout Entry
excerpt: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka skip preliminary rounds in both men's and women's cricket at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, with an India-Pakistan clash possible only from the semi-finals.
body:
• India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka have been given direct entry into the quarter-finals of both men's and women's T20 cricket at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.
  • An India-Pakistan men's match is possible only if both teams win their quarter-finals and are drawn on the same side of the bracket.
  • Shreyas Iyer captains the Indian men's squad, with Jasprit Bumrah and Tilak Varma among the marquee names; Harmanpreet Kaur leads the women's side.
  • The women's tournament runs September 17-22, with the men's event from September 24 to October 1.

The cricket draws for the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, were officially confirmed on Thursday, with India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka securing direct entry into the knockout stages of both the men's and women's tournaments, according to Reuters.

Men's Draw: Six Teams Fight for Remaining Spots

The 10-team men's competition begins with a preliminary round on September 24 featuring six associate and lower-ranked teams split into two groups. Afghanistan, Japan and Nepal were drawn in Group A, while Hong Kong, Malaysia and Oman form Group B. The top two teams from each group will advance to the quarter-finals to join the four seeded Full Member nations, according to CricTracker.

The format means an India-Pakistan men's clash is not guaranteed. The two teams can only meet if both win their respective quarter-finals and are drawn on the same side of the bracket — making a potential encounter possible in the semi-finals or the final, scheduled for October 1.

Women's Draw: India Face Hosts Japan

The women's tournament, running from September 17 to 22, features eight teams in a direct knockout format. Defending champions India will open their title defence against hosts Japan in the quarter-finals. Bangladesh take on China, Sri Lanka meet Malaysia, and Pakistan face Thailand in the other matchups, according to Cricket Addictor.

Should India overcome Japan, they would face either Bangladesh or China in the semi-finals, keeping a potential India-Pakistan women's final alive only if both teams advance through their respective halves of the draw.

Star-Studded Indian Squads

The BCCI has named strong squads for both tournaments. Shreyas Iyer leads the men's team with Tilak Varma as vice-captain. The squad features Jasprit Bumrah, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Abhishek Sharma and Arshdeep Singh, according to the Sporting News.

"India swept the cricket gold medals at the 2022 Asian Games, held in 2023 in Hangzhou, claiming both the men's and women's titles."

— Reuters

Harmanpreet Kaur captains the women's squad, with Smriti Mandhana as vice-captain. Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Deepti Sharma and Richa Ghosh are among the 15-member squad. All matches will be played at Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi prefecture, in the T20 format with full international status.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian cricket fans in Japan — one of the fastest-growing Indian diaspora communities in Asia — the tournament offers a rare chance to watch top-tier international cricket on home soil. The possibility of an India-Pakistan semi-final or final in Nagoya would add further intrigue to a tournament India enters as defending double gold medallists. Cricket returns to the Asian Games for the fourth time, having featured in 2010, 2014 and 2022.
